chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Abdullah ibn Sinan said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Who is rejected among the witnesses?' He said, 'The presumptuous (al-zhanin) and the suspected (al-mutaham).' I said, 'Then what about the corrupt (al-fasiq) and the treacherous (al-kha'in)?' He said, 'All of that falls under the presumptuous (al-zhanin).'

key_terms.الظَّنِينُ: The presumptuous one (one who assumes good without sufficient proof)
key_terms.وَالْخَائِنُ: The treacherous one (one who is untrustworthy)
key_terms.وَالْفَاسِقُ: The corrupt one (one who is known for sin or minor defects)
key_terms.وَالْمُتََّمُ: The suspected one (one who is suspected of a defect)

ai.seo_question: What are the criteria for rejecting witnesses in Shia jurisprudence according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a hierarchical framework for witness credibility, identifying 'al-zhanin' (those prone to suspicion) and 'al-mutahin' (the suspected) as the primary grounds for rejection. He clarifies that specific moral defects like being 'fasiq' (corrupt) or 'kha'in' (treacherous) are not separate categories but are subsumed under the broader epistemological category of 'al-zhanin,' reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on the reliability of testimony based on probable knowledge. This definition aligns with the principle that witness validity is contingent upon the absence of factors that induce doubt in their testimony.
